answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so influence requires paths supported by independent attestations. A sybil cluster with sparse external edges has low conductance, φ(S)=cut(S,¬S)/vol(S); under degree-weighted sampling, its chance of escaping in t steps is bounded by tφ(S). Thus min-cut and transitivity limits constrain its aggregate voting weight, rather than letting many linked identities amplify one another. A crystal, mirror, or willow label cannot alter that graph bound.
